newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS- SHORT-DATED DLR/YEN VOLS UP ON SPOT SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- SHORT-DATED DLR/YEN VOLS UP ON SPOT SLIDE.

text.p: Implied volatilities on short-dated dollar/yen options were firmer, with vols showing a renewed burst of energy following spot dollar/yen's drop of over four yen on Friday.

Traders said the market had settled down a bit since the fall in spot dollar/yen had come to a halt, but one-month vols were still at 12.10/40 percent at 1130 GMT, up from 11.20/70 seen in late European trade on Friday.

Spot dollar/yen had come off its session lows of 114.25 yen to trade one and a half yen above that level, but was still well below Friday's high at 118.63. The U.S. currency was buoyed as the market was still seeing the broad picture for the dollar as positive as U.S. economic fundamentals outshine those of Germany and Japan.

Vols for longer-term dollar/yen options softened as the market saw spot dollar/yen slip back following a rally which began late last month. Six-month vols were at 11.70/12.00 percent against Friday's 11.90/12.10, while one-year vols fell to 11.80/90 from 12.10/30.
"Until recently, there were a lot of dollar calls at around 125 yen and longer-dated vols were quite high," Yoshihisa Yamanaka, forex options manager at Sanwa Bank in London.
"But since the end of last week spot yen has strengthened, and this has led to a bit of selling pressure in the three-, six- and 12-month vols," Yamanaka said.
Following the turnaround in spot dollar/yen, its risk reversal, or the differential between put and call pricing, switched accordingly.
Dollar/yen 25-delta risk reversals were at 0.2/0.5 and tilted towards yen calls, shifting from 0.4/0.7 in favour of yen puts seen on Friday.
Meanwhile, in dollar/mark, although the spot rate suffered a fall that was as spectacular as that of dollar/yen on Friday, there was very little action in dollar/mark vols this morning.
After falling four pfennigs on Friday, spot dollar/mark was well off its lows at 1.8545/55, but was below its Friday highs of 1.8764 and the eight-year peak of 1.8913 seen last week.

"The situation today's not like when dollar/mark and dollar/yen were going higher and vols were really pumped. But if we get a spike back up towards the old highs we saw last week, we could easily see vols jump out of their skins," said a trader at a Canadian bank in London.
Dollar/mark vols eased across the board, with one-month quoted at 11.20/35 percent against Friday's 11.20/60, while one-year was at 11.20/40 against 11.40/60.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities softened as the spot rates calmed down after the pound's nosedive against the dollar and mark late last week.
One month sterling/mark vols dropped to 11.70/20 percent from Friday's 12.40/90, while one-month cable was at 10.40/70 against 10.70/11.10.
Mark/yen vols picked up after spot fell to 25-month lows earlier in the day. One-month vols firmed to 11.70/00 percent from Friday's 11.20/70, although one-year vols were unchanged at 10.60/80.
